CISA KEV: CVE-2026-34926 — Trend Micro Apex One (On-Premise) Directory Traversal Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-21 1 use case 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Trend Micro Apex One (on-premise) contains a directory traversal vulnerability that could allow a pre-authenticated local attacker to modify a key table on the server to inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations. Vendor: Trend Micro, Product: Apex One. Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.

Mini Shai Hulud: Compromised @antv npm packages enable CI/CD credential theft

Microsoft Security BlogStepSecurity
2026-05-20 13 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud durabletask dropper C2 callback to git-service.com Command & Control High
Detects outbound connections to the TeamPCP-controlled domains check.git-service.com / git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com or the hosting IP 160.119.64.3, particularly when initiated by a python3 process — the durabletask malicious __init__.py uses urllib.request.urlretrieve against check.git-service.com to fetch rope.pyz. Rationale: Domains check.git-service.com, git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com and IP 160.119.64.3 are explicit campaign IOCs in the Microsoft post. The article ties t.m-kosche[.]com to TeamPCP's broader Mini Shai-Hulud campaign that also hit TanStack, Mistral AI, LiteLLM and @antv — so these are high-fidelity even outside the durabletask scope.

[LLM] durabletask second-stage dropper: python3 executing /tmp/managed.pyz Installation High
Detects execution of /tmp/managed.pyz by python3 — the rope.pyz cloud-intrusion framework dropped to /tmp/managed.pyz by the compromised durabletask __init__.py. The dropper spawns four parallel child instances within ~4 seconds. Rationale: The article gives the exact dropper code (`subprocess.Popen(["python3","/tmp/managed.pyz"], ...)`) and the Harden-Runner process tree confirms /tmp/managed.pyz as the canonical second-stage path. This string is unique to TeamPCP's tooling.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] gh CLI token enumeration via python parent (managed.pyz credential exfil) Actions on Objectives High
Detects `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` invocations whose parent is python3 or whose grandparent is /tmp/managed.pyz — the credential-access path used by all four parallel rope.pyz collector instances to harvest GitHub tokens. Rationale: The Harden-Runner process tree in the article shows each of the 4 managed.pyz children running `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` back-to-back. Pairing those exact subcommands with a python parent makes the detection nearly FP-free outside of legitimate Python-based GH automation.

[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd user persistence Installation High
Detects creation of a systemd user unit named pgsql-monitor.service or invocation of `systemctl --user daemon-reload` by a python process — the persistence mechanism rope.pyz installs to survive runner restarts. The fake unit masquerades as a Postgres monitoring service. Rationale: The article explicitly names `pgsql-monitor.service` as the persistence artifact and shows `systemctl --user daemon-reload` in every one of the 4 managed.pyz child processes. The service name is highly specific to this campaign — legitimate PostgreSQL monitoring uses entirely different unit names (postgresql-exporter, prometheus-postgres-exporter, pg_stat_monitor, etc.).

[LLM] Single python parent fans out 3+ managed.pyz children within seconds Installation High
Detects the rope.pyz signature behaviour: one `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent that spawns 3+ child `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` processes within a 60s window. The article documents 4 parallel collector instances completing credential theft in under 4 seconds — this temporal/fan-out shape is rare outside the campaign. Rationale: The Harden-Runner process tree in the article documents exactly 4 managed.pyz children (PIDs 2380, 2404, 2430, 2432) under a single `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent, with the entire chain completing in <4 seconds. Threshold of ≥3 children within 60s is well below the observed fan-out — legitimate multiprocessing apps don't use this path/name.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1106
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildCount = count(),
            FirstChild = min(Timestamp),
            LastChild = max(Timestamp),
            ChildPIDs = make_set(ProcessId, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| extend SpawnWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastChild, FirstChild)
| where ChildCount >= 3 and SpawnWindowSec <= 60
| order by FirstChild desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| summarize ChildCount = count(),
            FirstChild = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastChild = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| extend SpawnWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastChild, FirstChild)
| where ChildCount >= 3 and SpawnWindowSec <= 60
| order by FirstChild desc

| ChildCount >= 3

| where spawn_window_sec <= 60

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where count >= 3
| eval spawn_window_sec = lastTime - firstTime
| where spawn_window_sec <= 60
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-05-20 13 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 analyzes TamperedChef malware clusters that use trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads to targets. The post Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse appeared first on Unit 42 .

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) · [LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags · [LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) Installation High
Hunts execution of binaries signed by the five disposable LLCs Unit 42 attributes to the CL-UNK-1090 TamperedChef cluster: CANDY TECH LTD, G.R.CIGAR. LTD, TAU CENTAURI LTD, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD, METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC. These shell entities exist solely to obtain Authenticode certs for trojanized PDF/recipe/calendar productivity apps; legitimate software from these company names does not exist. Rationale: The five LLC signer strings come directly from the Unit 42 table mapping CL-UNK-1090 binaries to their shell-company signers. These names are unique to the cluster and don't appear in legitimate software publishers. Confirmed against Sophos and WithSecure reporting that the operators rotate cert-issuing LLCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/tamperedchef • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1588.003 T1036.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          Signer = coalesce(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName),
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ParentProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Signer = coalesce(ActingProcessFileCompany, ParentProcessFileCompany),
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains Command & Control High
Hunts host network egress and DNS to the article's named TamperedChef infrastructure: appsuites.ai (including pdf-tool / vault subdomains), crystalpdf.com, freeonlinetools.info. These are the trojanized-installer download hosts and the dormant-then-activate C2 used by CL-CRI-1089 / CL-UNK-1090. Rationale: appsuites.ai, pdf-tool.appsuites.ai, vault.appsuites.ai, crystalpdf.com and freeonlinetools.info are the article's named distribution/C2 hosts; fullpdf.com added from Sophos corroboration. These are unique campaign-specific domains — no legitimate business overlap. Any callback after the dormancy window is high-confidence post-install activation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/tamperedchef-malware-disguised-as-fake.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tamperedchef-infostealer-delivered-through-fraudulent-pdf-editor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
  | extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
  | where Host in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Host endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Host endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "Network", Indicator = RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Query = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString))
  | where Query in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Query endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Query endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "DNS", Indicator = Query, RemoteIP = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".appsuites.ai" or DnsQuery endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (TamperedChefHosts) or DestinationHostName has_any (TamperedChefHosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, DnsQuery = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags Installation High
Hunts the article's productivity-app installers (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) re-launching themselves with the activation flags --cm, --install, --enableupdate or --fullupdate. These flags are the documented switch from dormant-installed state to active stealer/C2 behaviour and have no legitimate productivity-software analogue. Rationale: Article names AppSuite PDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky and CrystalPDF as the trojanized productivity apps. Sophos/Acronis/SecurityOnline corroborate --cm as the documented activation argument and --enableupdate / --fullupdate / --install as the persistent-update flags; these strings don't appear in legitimate productivity-app installers and pair directly with the article's family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/

[LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) Installation High
Hunts the article-corroborated TamperedChef persistence pattern: schtasks.exe importing a freshly-dropped task.xml that registers a recurring task launching wscript/cscript against an obfuscated JS such as appsuite-print.js. Combines the file-drop, the schtasks /create /xml import and the resulting script-host execution to catch the persistence handoff. Rationale: task.xml drop + schtasks /create /xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) is the TamperedChef persistence handoff documented by SecurityOnline and Acronis corroborating the article's CL-CRI-1089 trojanized-app behaviour. The 24h join window catches the schedule registration paired to the subsequent script-host launch, dramatically reducing FP vs schtasks alone. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/ • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            SchedCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            SchedParentCompany = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let ScriptHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, ScriptCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DeviceName
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DeviceName, AccountName,
          SchedParent, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            SchedCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParentName = ParentProcessName,
            SchedParentCompany = ParentProcessFileCompany;
let ScriptHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ScriptCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = ParentProcessName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DvcHostname
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          SchedParentName, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*"/create"* AND *"/xml"*) (@CommandLine:*task.xml* OR @CommandLine:*AppSuite* OR @CommandLine:*CrystalPDF* OR @CommandLine:*Calendaromatic* OR @CommandLine:*JustAskJacky* OR @CommandLine:*appsuite-print.js*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/create", field=CommandLine)
| regex("/xml", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(task\\.xml|AppSuite|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|appsuite-print\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

status: experimental

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

[LLM] BadIIS demo.pdb variant known SHA256 file/process hashes Installation High
Detects known BadIIS samples from the Talos demo.pdb commodity ecosystem by exact SHA256 hash on file write, image load, or process execution events. High-confidence retroactive sweep across all hosts. Rationale: Uses the 8 SHA256 IOCs published verbatim in the Talos article. Cross-checked against Elastic's BADIIS write-up and Trend Micro's earlier reporting confirming the same family lineage. Hash matching is article-specific and zero-FP if a hit occurs. Pivots across DNS, network-connection, and proxy telemetry. Rationale: Five IPs and two domains (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) published in the article. These are operational C2 — any contact is a high-fidelity signal. Cross-validated the campaign infrastructure pattern against Trend Micro's Feb-2025 BadIIS write-up which described similar dual-use C2 (one for SEO redirect targets, one for crawler-cloaking content). [LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) initiating outbound connection to public IP Command & Control Medium
Hunts for IIS application-pool worker processes (w3wp.exe) making outbound connections to the public internet. Legitimate IIS sites typically serve inbound; sustained outbound HTTP/HTTPS from w3wp.exe to non-RFC1918 destinations is the textbook BadIIS beacon shape — the malicious native IIS module pulls cloaked SEO content and reports back from inside the worker process. Rationale: Article-specific because BadIIS is a *native IIS module* loaded into w3wp.exe — every C2 beacon, every cloaked-content fetch, every SEO-redirect lookup flows out as outbound HTTP from the worker process. Elastic and Trend Micro both describe the module reaching a backend for crawler-decision content, confirming the egress pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/

| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(RemoteIP), SampleUrl=any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort

| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), SampleHost=any(DstHostname), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc

[LLM] IIS native module DLL drop or applicationHost.config modification by non-IIS process Installation High
Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module load paths (System32\inetsrv, Microsoft.NET\Framework64) or modifications to applicationHost.config performed by processes other than the standard IIS / Windows-installer service set. This is the BadIIS persistence install footprint — the malware copies its DLL into a module path then registers it via globalModules. Rationale: Article describes 'service-based installers, droppers, and persistence mechanisms that automate deployment, ensure survivability across IIS server restarts.' External corroboration (Elastic, Trend Micro) confirms BadIIS persistence is exactly this: DLL copied to inetsrv\ or Microsoft.NET\Framework64\ + applicationHost.config edited to register the module. Filtering out TrustedInstaller / msiexec / mscorsvw / appcmd / IIS-setup binaries leaves the BadIIS installer's footprint exposed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://www.welivesecurity.com/2021/08/06/anatomy-native-iis-malware/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1543.003

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\inetsrv\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or FileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFile = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
    | where (TargetFilePath has @"\inetsrv\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or TargetFileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="FileEvent", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let SuspectProcess = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "appcmd.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install module","add module","/section:globalModules","/section:modules")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ProcessCreate", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
union SuspectFile, SuspectProcess
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) writing robots.txt / .php / .js into web root Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects IIS worker process writing or modifying SEO-fraud artifact files (robots.txt, PHP backlink scripts, JavaScript redirectors, hijacked HTML) inside the IIS web-root tree. Legitimate IIS workers serve files; only a malicious in-process module writes content back into wwwroot — the exact SEO-fraud and content-hijacking behaviour the Talos article describes including 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' and 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts'. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' as a malware feature folder, plus 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts' as the builder's output. w3wp.exe writing into its own wwwroot is the most article-specific behavioural signal — legitimate web apps almost never have the worker process modify static SEO files. Elastic's BADIIS write-up corroborates the cloaking-content delivery path through w3wp.exe. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\" and FileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "w3wp.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
| where (TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (TargetFileName endswith ".php" or TargetFileName endswith ".js" or TargetFileName endswith ".html" or TargetFileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\" and TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133") or RemoteUrl has_any ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Service Persistence via sc.exe with User-Writable Path
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0e
status: experimental
description: |
    sc.exe create with the binary path under \Users\, \AppData\,
    \ProgramData\, or \Temp\ — service-install persistence outside
    legitimate program directories.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1543.003
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_sc:
        Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'create'
    selection_path:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Users\'
            - '\AppData\'
            - '\ProgramData\'
            - '\Temp\'
    condition: selection_sc and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Internal install scripts dropping a service from %ProgramData%
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again. Mass npm Supply Chain Attack Hits the AntV Ecosystem

StepSecurity
2026-05-19 16 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A new wave of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm has compromised packages across Alibaba's AntV data visualization ecosystem, echarts-for-react, timeago.js, and dozens more. Stolen CI/CD secrets are being dumped to thousands of public GitHub repositories as the attack continues to spread.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised AntV / Shai-Hulud npm package version landed in node_modules · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again. Mass npm Supply Chain Attack Hits the AntV Ecosyst
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Persistence backdoor: node/npm writes to Claude Code or VS Code user config · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud C2 beacon to t.m-kosche.com (OpenTelemetry decoy) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog spawned by Node/npm lifecycle on dev workstation or CI runner · [LLM] Process fan-out reading 130+ cloud-credential / wallet paths in short window · [LLM] GitHub repo created with reversed Shai-Hulud signature in description · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Shai-Hulud C2 beacon to t.m-kosche.com (OpenTelemetry decoy) Command & Control High
Detects outbound DNS/HTTPS connections to the Mini Shai-Hulud fallback C2 t.m-kosche.com — disguised as an OpenTelemetry collector endpoint. Process context (node.exe, npm, GitHub Actions runner) raises confidence the call came from an infected install/CI step rather than a legitimate telemetry consumer. Rationale: t.m-kosche.com is the named C2 domain in the article and is corroborated by JFrog, Microsoft, Snyk, Socket and Chainguard — single-source-only domains were dropped. Disguising as OpenTelemetry makes it survive naïve allow-lists but the FQDN is unique enough to anchor an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://socket.dev/blog/antv-packages-compromised • https://www.chainguard.dev/unchained/mini-shai-hulud-npm-attack-antv-ecosystem-compromise-may-2026
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1001.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let C2Hosts = dynamic(["t.m-kosche.com","m-kosche.com"]);
union
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Hosts) or RemoteUrl endswith ".m-kosche.com"
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId),
  (DeviceEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
   | where AdditionalFields has_any (C2Hosts)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName,
             InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId)
| extend SuspiciousParent = iff(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Listener.exe"), true, false)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let C2Hosts = dynamic(["t.m-kosche.com","m-kosche.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where DnsQuery has_any (C2Hosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".m-kosche.com"
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsQueryType, EventProduct),
  (ImNetworkSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where DstHostname has_any (C2Hosts) or Url has_any (C2Hosts)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, EventProduct),
  (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where Name has_any (C2Hosts) or Name endswith ".m-kosche.com"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TruffleHog spawned by Node/npm lifecycle on dev workstation or CI runner Actions on Objectives High
Mini Shai-Hulud downloads and executes TruffleHog from within the npm install/postinstall context to scan the home directory for cloud, source-control and wallet credentials. Legitimate TruffleHog use is almost always invoked by CI step names or developers directly — not by node.exe/npm spawning it mid-install. The parent-child pair is the article-specific anchor. Rationale: Multiple corroborating sources (Microsoft Security Blog, JFrog, Socket) confirm the payload runs TruffleHog from within the install/postinstall hook. Restricting to node/npm/Runner parents drops legitimate dev usage which is normally launched from a shell or CI step name. High-fidelity behavioural anchor that survives even if the C2 changes. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://socket.dev/blog/antv-packages-compromised • https://safedep.io/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-314-npm-packages-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.007 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "trufflehog.exe" or FileName =~ "trufflehog"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git","trufflehog github","trufflehog --json")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","corepack.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Listener.exe","bash.exe","sh")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","yarn install","pnpm install","npx ","@antv/","timeago.js","echarts-for-react")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("trufflehog","trufflehog.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git","trufflehog github")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","Runner.Worker.exe","bash.exe","sh")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","yarn install","pnpm install","@antv/","timeago.js")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
title: TruffleHog Spawned by Node.js / npm Lifecycle (Shai-Hulud Indicator)
id: 6e1f9a47-3b6c-4a51-b6ec-7d99b30b7c0e
description: Detects the legitimate TruffleHog secret-scanner being executed as a child of node/npm/yarn/pnpm or a GitHub Actions Runner — the exact behaviour used by Mini Shai-Hulud to harvest creds from the home directory during package install.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem
  - https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\trufflehog.exe'
      - '/trufflehog'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npx.cmd'
      - '\yarn.cmd'
      - '\pnpm.cmd'
      - '\Runner.Worker.exe'
      - '/node'

[LLM] Process fan-out reading 130+ cloud-credential / wallet paths in short window Actions on Objectives High
The Shai-Hulud payload harvests credentials from over 130 file paths spanning AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, crypto wallets and developer tools. Legitimate code rarely touches more than a handful of these per session. This UC fires when a single process opens many distinct credential-bearing paths within a tight window — a high-fidelity proxy for the harvest stage. Rationale: Article and Microsoft/JFrog/Socket independently list the 130+ paths covering AWS, GCP, Azure, K8s, Vault, wallets and dev tools. A threshold on distinct paths per process within minutes is the cleanest behavioural shape — survives obfuscation changes because the harvest target list itself is the IOC. Sigma omitted: detection requires counting/dcount which isn't single-event-shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/ • https://socket.dev/blog/antv-packages-compromised • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/

[LLM] Persistence backdoor: node/npm writes to Claude Code or VS Code user config Installation Medium
The Shai-Hulud payload plants persistent backdoors in Claude Code and VS Code configurations so the implant survives across sessions. Legitimate writes to these paths come from the IDE itself or the user — not from npm/node lifecycle scripts. The pivot is the (node/npm/yarn parent) → (write to ~/.claude or VS Code user-settings/extensions) pair. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out Claude Code and VS Code config tampering as a persistence mechanism — that's an unusual TTP shape and a strong fingerprint. Restricting the write parent to node/npm/yarn excludes the IDEs themselves writing their own configs (Code.exe, Claude.exe). Multi-source confirmed by Microsoft and Snyk write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem

[LLM] GitHub repo created with reversed Shai-Hulud signature in description Actions on Objectives High
After credential theft, the worm creates public GitHub repositories using stolen tokens, naming them with Dune-universe terminology and describing them with the reversed string "niagA oG eW ereH :duluH-iahS". Detecting this against the org's audit log surfaces exfil-by-token activity hours/days after the initial compromise. Rationale: "niagA oG eW ereH :duluH-iahS" is the article's literal, reversed signature string — confirmed by JFrog and Phoenix Security (2,200+ to 2,500+ repos). Combined with Dune-themed names this is essentially zero-FP. Sentinel left blank because GitHub audit logs reach Sentinel only via custom connector tables (GitHub_CL etc.) which aren't in the canonical schema. Falcon/CloudWatch N/A — not endpoint or AWS-CloudTrail telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/ • https://phoenix.security/teampcp-mini-shai-hulud-npm-atool-maintainer-compromise-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/antv-packages-compromised • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, CountryCode,

[LLM] Compromised AntV / Shai-Hulud npm package version landed in node_modules Delivery High
Detects the specific malicious package versions hitting the file system as they're installed into node_modules — anchored on the exact package@version strings from the article (timeago.js@4.1.2/4.2.2, @antv/g2@5.5.8/5.6.8, echarts-for-react@3.0.7/3.1.7/3.2.7, etc.) and on the two confirmed SHA256 payload hashes. Rationale: Article supplies the exact package@version matrix and two SHA256 hashes; both hashes are confirmed by JFrog and Socket. Hash hit = critical; path hit alone is medium because legitimate (older or non-compromised) versions of these packages do exist. Sigma is hash-only (single-event shape); path-based detection emits via the SIEM queries.   "@antv/s2@2.8.1","@antv/s2@2.9.1",
  "@antv/x6@3.2.7","@antv/x6@3.3.7",
  "@antv/l7@2.26.10","@antv/l7@2.27.10"
]);
union
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where SHA256 in (BadHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName, MatchReason = "sha256"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
   | where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)node_modules[\\/](@antv[\\/][^\\/]+|timeago\.js|timeago-react|echarts-for-react|jest-canvas-mock|jest-date-mock|size-sensor|canvas-nest\.js|filesize\.js|onfire\.js|relationship\.js|ribbon\.js|slice\.js|word-width|lint-md|lint-md-cli|mcp-echarts|mcp-mermaid|@lint-md[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]package\.json$"
   | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
   | extend PkgJsonPath = FolderPath
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName, MatchReason = "path-of-compromised-package")
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let BadHashes = dynamic([
  "a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c",
  "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where (Hash in (BadHashes) or TargetFileSHA256 in (BadHashes))
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)node_modules[\\/](@antv[\\/][^\\/]+|timeago\.js|timeago-react|echarts-for-react|jest-canvas-mock|jest-date-mock|size-sensor|canvas-nest\.js|@lint-md[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]package\.json$"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
